hints.title: Key Ordering Elimination Obstacle
hints.text: In an ordered search tree, all left subtree values are strictly smaller and all right subtree values are strictly larger. How can comparing the target with the current value eliminate half the search space at each step?

hints.title: BST Routing Invariant
hints.text: At each step, if target equals current value, return the node. If target is smaller, search left; if larger, search right.

hints.title: Iterative Traversal Procedure
hints.text: Start at root while node is not null. If val == node.val, return node. If val < node.val, move to node.left. Otherwise, move to node.right. Return null if the search space is exhausted.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: H: height of BST (log N on average, N worst-case)
complexity.notes: Iterative pointer traversal descending at most height H steps with zero auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Uninformed tree traversal inspects all N nodes taking O(N) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterative implementation uses O(1) space versus O(H) call stack for recursive traversal.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using iterative traversal to guarantee O(1) space.
